title: Ad Felicem Notarium De Trinitate Liber Unus
author: Fulgentius of Ruspe
source: Translated by Claude from stoa0128b.stoa009.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.

passages.original: Audiat Sabeliius sumus, audiat tres, et credat esse tres personas, et non sacrilego corde blasphemet, dicendo ipsum sibi esse Patrem, ipsum sibi Filium, ipsum sibi Spiritum sanctum: tanquam modo quodam seipsum gignat, aut modo quodam a seipso ipse procedat; cum hoc etiam in naturis creatis minime inveniro possit, ut aliquid seipsum gignere valeat. Audiat scilicet et Arius, Unum, et non differentis Filium dicat esse naturæ, cum natura diversa unum dici nequeat. Filius itaque clamat, Ego et Pater unum sumus (Joan. x, 30); et : Qui me videt, videt et Patrem (Joan. XIV, 9). Et Apostolus de eo: Qui cum in forma Dei, inquit, esset, non rapinam arbitratus est esse se æqualem Deo (Philip. II, 6) ; et : Propterea, inquit in Evangelio, quærebant Judæi Jesum interficere, quia non solum solvebat sabbatum, sed et Patrem suum dicebat Deum, æqualem se faciens Deo (Joan. v, 18). Et Arius blasphemo spiritu contradicit: Non sun unum, non sunt æquales, quia ipse Filius de se dicit: Pater major me est (Joan. XIV, 28); et missum sese sæpenumero a Patre testatur.
passages.english: Let Sabellius hear "we are," let him hear "three," and let him believe that there are three persons, and not blaspheme with a sacrilegious heart by saying that the same one is Father to himself, the same one Son to himself, the same one Holy Spirit to himself, as though in some manner he begets himself, or in some manner he himself proceeds from himself; since this cannot be found even in created natures, that anything should be able to beget itself. Let Arius likewise hear "one," and not say that the Son is of a different nature, since a diverse nature cannot be called one. And so the Son cries out, "I and the Father are one" (John 10:30); and: "Whoever sees me sees the Father also" (John 14:9). And the Apostle [says] of him: "Who, though he was in the form of God," he says, "did not consider it robbery to be equal to God" (Philippians 2:6); and: "For this reason," it says in the Gospel, "the Jews sought to kill Jesus, because he not only broke the sabbath, but also called God his own Father, making himself equal to God" (John 5:18). And Arius contradicts with a blasphemous spirit: "They are not one, they are not equal, because the Son himself says of himself, 'The Father is greater than I' (John 14:28); and he frequently testifies that he was sent by the Father."
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: "Sabeliius" for Sabellius, "inveniro" for inveniri, "sun" for sunt. "Sumus" and "tres" refer back to the quoted words "we are" (John 10:30) and "three" (1 John 5:7) in the preceding context.
